To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the structure of FixK-DNA complexes reveals the molecular basis of DNA binding and explains how oxidation of the cysteinyl thiol of FixK interferes with DNA binding and transcription activation.
the structure of FixK-DNA reveals the DNA-binding site and explains how oxidation of the single, conserved cysteine interferes with transcriptional activation of the FixK regulon.
the structure of the Fixk2 protein-DNA complex reveals the DNA-binding site and explains how the oxidation of the surface-exposed cystein thiol interferes with DNA binding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of how a transcriptional activator of the CRP family is negatively controlled by a single cysteine residue.
the structure of a FixK protein and its DNA complex, which provides a basis for the elucidation of the regulatory mechanisms of FixK2.
the elucidation of the structural basis of DNA binding of FixK2 and the role of Cys-183 in FixK2 function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structure of the Fixk2-DNA complex explains the mechanism of how FixK2 activity is controlled by post-translational modification and proteolysis.
FixK2 is an active transcriptional regulator, but only under conditions of a reduced redox environment.
the FixK2 structure provides a molecular explanation of how oxidation and proteolysis interfere with the DNA-binding activity of FixK and how the FixK-DNA interaction is regulated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FixK2 represents a new type of CRP family protein that is controlled by oxidation of a surface cysteine.
the structure of the FixJ-FixK2-DNA ternary complex explains how a single cysteine residue can be used as a switch to regulate transcription.
a FixK2-DNACys183S-His6 protein complex is formed that can be crystallized, which allowed for the determination of the three-dimensional structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
post-translational oxidation is a means to control transcriptional activation by FixK2 and, by extension, by other members of this subgroup of the CRPs.
the FixK2 structure provides an explanation for the negative control of this transcription factor by post-translational modification.
the structure of FixK-DNA complexes explains how a posttranslational modification of FixK proteins by reactive oxygen species can be used to shut off gene transcription.
